(Scope of work) Scope of work :- 1. Project Background & Objective Hindustan Copper Limited (HCL), Indian Copper Complex (ICC), intends to execu te water conservation-related civil works. The primary objective is the construc tion of a Check Dam in a nearby village of Surda under the approved Re mediation Plan. The work aims to facilitate water harvesting and groundwater recharge in the surrounding village area using site-appropriate masonry method s. 2. Detailed Scope of Activities The successful bidder shall be responsible for executing all civil works necessary for the complete construction and protection of the Check Dam. The scope inclu des, but is not limited to, the following activities as per the itemized bill of quant ities: Earthwork and Excavation: Excavation of foundation trenches in all kind s of soil profiles (including soil mixed with gravel, slag, boulders, etc.) up to the required depths, including watering, backfilling with approved quality s oil , ramming, and consolidating. Stone Rubble Masonry: Construction of the core check dam structure usi ng random rubble masonry in Cement Mortar (1:4). Material Sourcing: Stones/boulders are to be collected and utilized fro m the river as permitted for this work. Execution: The contractor's scope includes collection, handling, dressi ng/breaking, internal/external transportation, and layout execution of the stone masonry work. Concrete Works: Providing and laying Plain Cement Concrete (PCC) of grade 1:3:6 (1 c ement : 3 coarse sand : 6 graded stone aggregate 40mm nominal siz e) for foundations up to plinth level. Providing and laying Reinforced Cement Concrete (RCC) of grade 1:1. 5:3 (1 cement : 1.5 coarse sand : 3 graded stone aggregate 20mm no minal size) for structural components up to plinth level (excluding the cost of reinforcement and shuttering). Formwork: Providing, erecting, propping, and removing centering and sh uttering for concrete work Stone Pitching: Laying 22.5 cm thick dry stone pitching in proper courses and profiles using hammer-dressed stones (with no side less than 15 cm an d a minimum depth of 20 cm). Sand Filling: Supplying, filling, spreading, leveling, watering, and rammin g best available local sand under floors and plinths. Boulder Supply: Supplying, filling, spreading, and leveling toe boulders w ithin the size range of 5 cm to 20 cm for downstream erosion protection. Allied Protection: Providing and fixing G.I. Chain Link Fabric to engulf the stone pitching of required width (mesh size 50x50 mm), structurally str engthened with 2 mm diameter wire, nuts, bolts, and washers. Dewatering & Slush Management: Handling structural execution under challenging conditions, including pumping out water, mud, or liquid accum ulation from foundation trenches during excavation and concreting as requ ired.

3. Materials, Tools, and Plant (T&P) Contractor’s Responsibility: The contractor shall arrange all necessary t ools, tackles, construction machinery, concrete mixers, dewatering pumps, and shuttering materials required for the seamless execution of the work a t their own cost. Material Quality: All commercial construction materials (Cement, Sand, R einforcement Steel, G.I. Fencing, etc.) must comply with relevant Indian St andard (IS) codes and undergo approval by the HCL ICC Civil Department R epresentative prior to use. Stone Sourcing: Boulders/stones shall be sourced from the nearby river a rea designated by the local authorities/HCL, ensuring proper dressing to ac hieve structural stability. 4. Site Conditions and Special Directives Water & Mud Handling: Since the work involves check dam construction , the contractor must foresee water ingress in the working channels. Execu tion rates must accommodate necessary sub-surface or surface water pum ping. Levelling Course: A leveling course at the top of the random rubble maso nry structure must be completed with Cement Concrete (1:4:8) where desi gnated. Work Site: The work is situated near Surda village. The bidder is advised t o visit the site to familiarize themselves with local logistics, riverbed appro ach paths, and material handling leads before submitting their offer. 5. Period of Contract and Clean-up Completion Schedule: The work shall be completed within the timelines stipulated in the Notice Inviting Tender (NIT). Site Restoration: Upon completion of the construction, the contractor sha ll remove all balance debris, unused materials, and temporary setups, leavi ng the check dam site clean, dressed, and structurally sound for water con servation use. Annexure-II (PQC) PRE-QUALIFICATION CRITERIA: 1. Party must have to provide executed order copy/copies of successfully execut ed contract/s (Work Order/s) of Job contract for Civil Works related to constructio ns, maintenance, replacements, add-ons, renovation or remodeling of all existin g infrastructure in any CPWD/MES/ Railway/ Government of India undertaking/st ate Public Sector / listed companies having Company Identification Number (Not Private Limited) during last seven years ending last day of the month previous to the one in which offers are invited fulfilling either of the following: - (i) One (1) executed order copy of basic value not less than Rs 5.99 Lakhs for e ach (ii) Two (2) executed order copy of basic value not less than Rs. 3.75 lakhs for e

ach or (iii) Three (3) executed order copy of basic value not less than Rs. 2.99 lakhs for each Successful Job completion certificate where the reference of work order is menti oned is to be enclosed along with copy of such successfully executed contract fo r the requisite values of PQC point no. 1. i) OR 1. ii) OR 1. iii). 2. The Bidder shall have positive net worth as per their latest audited financial s tatement. Relevant documentary evidence including copies of Annual Report, co ntaining Profit & Loss Statement and Balance Sheets for immediate preceding th ree (3) consecutive accounting years ending March 2025 or the last date on whi ch the accounting year ends. Balance Sheet, Profit & Loss Account duly audited, stamped and signed by CA/CA Firm mentioning UDIN, FRN & MRN for Financial Y ear 2022-23 , 2023-24 and 2024-25 are to be enclosed. The Bidder should an average annual financial turnover of at least Rs. 2.25 Lakh s during the last 3 years, ending 31st March 2025. . 6. 3. The Seller shall, notwithstanding the consent and assignment/sub-contract, remain jointly and severally liable and responsible to buyer together with the assignee/ sub-contractor, for and in respect of the due performance of the Contract and the Sellers obligations there under.
